transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date/Time: 2028-02-27 14:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Recording ID: ff-20280227-northpoint-02
Attendees (Redwood): Liam Brooks (AE), Nina Patel (SE)
Attendees (Customer): Olivia Grant (Head of Search), Jon Meyer (ML Engineer), Priya Singh (Infra), Tom Alvarez (Product), Anya Kaur (Legal)
Shared links: demo deck: https://redwood.ai/sales/decks/northpoint-embeddings | sample bench: https://redwood.ai/sales/bench/northpoint-500k

AUTO SUMMARY: hosted embeddings + rerank demo, console tour of Optimize suggestions, discussed two-stage rerank, caching, quantization, security docs, pilot scope (500k docs), next steps and benchmark scheduling.

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Liam Brooks: Hey everyone thanks for making time, um quick intros, I'm Liam from Redwood and Nina is our SE.
[00:08] Olivia Grant: Hi all  Olivia here, head of search at NorthPoint. We want to see how a Redwood rerank fits with our current OpenSearch + Pinecone hybrid.
[00:18] Jon Meyer: Jon, ML eng. I'll be the person running the pilot and the benchmarks. Latency is, uh, big for us.
[00:25] Nina Patel: Great. Agenda  show embeddings endpoint, call flow for retrieval + rerank, Console Optimize suggestions, then Q&A and pilot planning.
[00:36] Tom Alvarez: Quick ask from Product  do you support explainability tokens or score breakdowns in responses?
[00:42] Nina Patel: Yes we return scores and an optional explain object per candidate; we can also return token-level highlights if needed.
[00:50] Priya Singh: Our SLO is 250ms P95 for search. Is hosted viable or do we need Dedicated?
[00:57] Liam Brooks: Hosted can meet that in many regions with warm pools and prefix caching; for very tight tails Dedicated is common. We'll show sample P95 numbers during the demo but actuals depend on candidate K and model variant.
[01:12] Anya Kaur: From legal, SOC2 and data residency are gating. We need to know about customer-managed keys and audit logs.
[01:20] Liam Brooks: Absolutely; hosted supports customer-managed KMS, audit log export, and region pinning. We'll attach security docs after this call.
[01:30] [screen share starts, faint audio overlap]
[01:35] Nina Patel: Ok demo time  here's a simplified flow: query -> embeddings -> vector store retrieval (top-K) -> Redwood rerank. We'll show two-stage pattern: cheap vector filter then strong reranker on top-10.
[01:52] [screen share] Nina Patel: Calling embeddings endpoint now - response returns embedding vector of 1536 dims in this model. Then we use our vector store to get top-200, do light post-filtering and call /rerank with top-20.
[02:12] Jon Meyer: Top-200 seems heavy; how much does cost jump if we push to top-200 then rerank top-20?
[02:19] Liam Brooks: Cost for rerank roughly scales with candidate count; we recommend a hybrid approach: use vector-sim prefilter to get top-N cheaply then run shrimp-you-know a smaller candidate list through the larger reranker. (laughter)
[02:34] Olivia Grant: There's a small transcription hiccup there but point's taken.
[02:38] Nina Patel: Sorry, I said "smaller stronger" model. Two-stage is common: cheap model for 200->20 then stronger model for 20->final.
[02:48] [05:00 mark jump - showing Console Optimize suggestions]
[05:02] Nina Patel: Console Optimize gives batch size suggestions, quantization profiles, and recommends model variants based on your token-length distribution. For example, if your average snippet length is 120 tokens we might suggest medium-short sequence kernels and 4-bit quantization for the rerank hot path.
[05:23] Tom Alvarez: Do you run automatic evals during model upgrades? We can't have relevance regressions in prod.
[05:30] Liam Brooks: Yes, Redwood Optimize ties evals to deployment jobs, can run holdout prompt sets and assert on metrics; we can auto-block rollouts that fail thresholds.
[05:42] Priya Singh: What about cold starts? We have unpredictable traffic spikes.
[05:46] Nina Patel: Warm pools, prewarmed instances, and autoscale policies help; for spikes we recommend a burst policy or Dedicated baseline for guaranteed capacity.
[05:58] [live API example at ~10 minute mark]
[10:03] Nina Patel: I'm making a live /rerank call with 12 candidates - current response time 148ms from EU region, includes network hop. Response includes score and explain tokens.
[10:20] Jon Meyer: Can you show the payload schema? We have payload size limits for our edge gateways.
[10:25] Nina Patel: Minimal rerank payload contains query, candidates array (id + snippet), and optional features dict. You can omit long text and pass short snippets for scoring; we support passing metadata only if you want to avoid large payloads.
[10:40] Olivia Grant: For the pilot, we are thinking 500k documents and expected monthly queries around 700k, peak QPS about 80. Is that reasonable?
[10:50] Liam Brooks: Yes, that's sensible. We'll run the cost model with those numbers and propose Hosted vs Dedicated and a hybrid option. We'll include sample SLO configs.
[11:05] Tom Alvarez: Any SDKs you recommend for managing candidate batching and truncation?
[11:10] Nina Patel: Python and Node SDKs include helper utilities to chunk candidates, pad/truncate snippets, and handle retries with backoff. We'll share code snippets after.
[11:24] [13:00 jump - deeper technical dive on scoring and structured features]
[13:02] Nina Patel: You can pass structured features like popularity, recency, or vendor boosts and the reranker will use them as signals. We expose a simple weighting mechanism in the schema.
[13:18] Jon Meyer: How do you version models and ensure determinism? Upgrades can shift embeddings a lot.
[13:25] Liam Brooks: Embeddings aren't guaranteed deterministic across major model changes. We advise pinning versions and running regression suites. Redwood provides a model catalog and rolling canary tooling.
[13:40] Anya Kaur: Legal question  can logs be redacted for PII?
[13:46] Liam Brooks: Yes logs are configurable and can be redacted or excluded; we support masking at ingestion and configurable retention windows.
[14:00] [17:00 mark - benchmarking conversation]
[17:05] Nina Patel: For the benchmark we'll need the sample docs, expected query mix, and a holdout set for relevance evaluation. Our template includes metrics to capture latency, cost per query, and MAP/NDCG.
[17:22] Jon Meyer: We'll provide a holdout of about 5k queries and relevance labels. Can Redwood run the eval or do we need to run locally?
[17:29] Liam Brooks: We can run it in a secured benchmarking environment or provide the scripts for you to run locally. For privacy-sensitive data, many customers prefer local runs with our script outputs compared afterwards.
[17:45] Priya Singh: If we do hosted, what about KMS? We need customer-managed keys in our EU account.
[17:52] Liam Brooks: Hosted supports customer-managed KMS and region pinning; Private deployment is available if you want full air-gapped control. We'll include the KMS integration guide.
[18:05] [22:00 quick demo of rollback mechanism]
[22:03] Nina Patel: Here's a canary rollback: we pushed a candidate model to 10% traffic and the evaluation metric dropped, console flagged it and auto-rolled back. This avoids large regressions.
[22:18] Tom Alvarez: Nice, that's useful.
[22:22] [28:00 - cost discussion and tips]
[28:05] Liam Brooks: Cost drivers are candidate K, context length, and model size. Tactics: run a cheap model first, quantize hot models, tune batch sizes, and use KV prefix caching for repeated contexts. Optimize will suggest those settings automatically.
[28:30] Olivia Grant: What monitoring do we get per-route?
[28:34] Nina Patel: Per-route dashboards: P95 latency, token counts, cost breakdown, error rates, and attribution by model version. You can set alerts on SLO breaches.
[28:48] Jon Meyer: For the pilot, do you provide an ingress pattern for bulk ingest?
[28:53] Liam Brooks: Yes, we have bulk ingest docs and partner connectors; we also provide migration patterns for Pinecone/OpenSearch to reduce downtime.
[29:05] [35:00 closing and recap]
[35:02] Liam Brooks: Recap: we'll send cost comparisons, security docs, benchmark template, and SDK examples. Nina will own the benchmark setup.
[35:18] Olivia Grant: We'll aim to share the 500k anonymized sample and query holdout by 3/5. Legal will follow up on SOC2 questions.
[35:30] Anya Kaur: Expect an email from me with a short compliance checklist.
[35:36] Liam Brooks: Great. We'll schedule the benchmark slot once we have the data. Thanks everyone.
[35:44] [meeting ended]
